description: Lifecycle Hooks configuration page — manages webhooks and actions triggered by execution events, with CRUD operations, enable/disable toggles, and hook testing capabilities.

groups.name: Hook Inventory and Status
groups.description: The Lifecycle Hooks page allows users to configure actions that execute automatically at specific points during workflow execution (e.g., on workflow start, completion, failure). Users need to see all configured hooks at a glance with their names, event triggers, enabled/disabled state, and any recent execution results. The page header shows the hook count and provides quick access to creating new hooks and refreshing the list. When no hooks exist, an informative empty state guides users to create their first hook rather than leaving them on a blank page.

assertions.description: Users can identify the Lifecycle Hooks page with a clear heading and subtitle explaining that hooks are actions configured to run at specific execution events

Users understand the purpose of hooks through a descriptive subtitle that explains they configure actions to run at execution events, providing context for users encountering this feature for the first time

criteria.textContent: Configure actions to run at specific execution events

assertions.description: When no hooks are configured, users see a helpful empty state with a clear call-to-action to create their first hook, explaining the value of lifecycle hooks rather than showing a blank list

groups.name: Hook Creation and Configuration
groups.description: Users need to create new hooks by specifying a name, URL endpoint, event triggers, custom headers, and payload configuration. The hook editor should open as a modal or panel when creating a new hook or editing an existing one. The save operation should validate the hook configuration and provide clear feedback on success or failure. Editing an existing hook should pre-populate the form with current values. The system should support both creating new hooks and updating existing ones through the same editor interface.

assertions.description: Users can create new lifecycle hooks by clicking a New Hook button, which opens an editor where they can configure the hook's name, URL, event triggers, headers, and payload format
Users can edit existing hooks by clicking an edit action on a hook card, which opens the editor pre-populated with the hook's current configuration for modification
Users can delete hooks they no longer need, with a confirmation dialog that clearly states the action is irreversible and shows the hook name being deleted

groups.name: Hook Testing and Toggle Controls
groups.description: Before relying on hooks in production workflows, users need to verify that their hook configurations work correctly. The test feature sends a sample payload to the configured URL and reports success/failure along with response details and execution duration. Additionally, hooks can be individually enabled or disabled without deletion, allowing users to temporarily suspend hook execution during maintenance or debugging without losing their configuration. These operational controls are essential for building confidence in the hook system and managing it in real development workflows.

assertions.description: Users can test individual hooks to verify connectivity and correct configuration, receiving a result that shows whether the test passed or failed along with the response and duration in milliseconds
Users can enable or disable individual hooks without deleting them, allowing temporary suspension of hook execution while preserving the configuration for future use
When hook operations fail, users see clear error messages with enough detail to diagnose the issue, and can dismiss errors after reading them

states.name: Loading Hooks
states.description: The page has just mounted and is fetching the list of configured lifecycle hooks from the backend. A loading indicator is shown while the request is in flight.

transitions.name: No hooks returned from backend
One or more hooks returned from backend
Backend request to fetch hooks fails

states.name: Empty State
states.description: No lifecycle hooks are configured. The page shows a helpful empty state message guiding the user to create their first hook. The New Hook button is available.

transitions.name: User clicks New Hook to create their first hook

states.name: Hook List
states.description: One or more lifecycle hooks are displayed in a list. Each hook card shows its name, event triggers, and enabled/disabled state. The page heading with hook count, the New Hook button, and per-hook action buttons (edit, test, toggle, delete) are available.

elements.textContains: Configure actions to run at specific execution events

transitions.name: User clicks New Hook to add another hook
User clicks edit on an existing hook card
User clicks delete on a hook card
User clicks test on a hook and the test completes
User toggles a hook enabled or disabled
A hook operation fails unexpectedly

states.name: Hook Editor
states.description: The hook editor modal or panel is open. When creating a new hook the form is empty; when editing an existing hook the form is pre-populated. The editor includes fields for hook name, URL endpoint, event triggers, custom headers, and payload configuration, along with Save and Cancel actions.

transitions.name: User saves the hook successfully
User cancels the editor and returns to the hook list
User cancels the editor and no hooks exist yet
Save operation fails with a validation or backend error

states.name: Delete Confirmation
states.description: A confirmation dialog is shown asking the user to confirm deletion of a specific hook. The dialog displays the hook name and warns that the action is irreversible, with Confirm and Cancel buttons.

transitions.name: User confirms deletion and hooks remain
User confirms deletion of the last hook
User cancels the deletion and returns to the hook list
Delete operation fails

states.name: Test Result Display
states.description: A hook test has completed and the result is displayed, showing whether the test passed or failed along with the response details and execution duration in milliseconds. The user can dismiss the result and return to the hook list.

transitions.name: User dismisses the test result and returns to the hook list

states.name: Error
states.description: An operation has failed and an error banner is displayed with details about the failure. The user can dismiss the error to return to the previous functional state.

transitions.name: User dismisses the error and hooks exist
User dismisses the error and no hooks exist
